document.title: feat(fonts): colour emoji from Twemoji in the glyph atlas
document.summary: Slice 3 of the glyph-cache design: CMake downloads the pinned Twemoji 72 px PNGs into the gitignored `assets/emoji`, and Text, Button and TextInput draw emoji clusters from them in colour through the existing RGBA8 atlas pages, or a fallback glyph when an image is missing.
document.why: The approved [design](source:s1) asks for full Unicode coverage including colour emoji, with Twemoji as the art, and [Máté's review](source:s2) asks for an emoji in the smoke golden. [Máté's change request](source:s3) asks to download the images at build time instead of committing them, with a fallback character when they are missing.

sources.title: Font glyph coverage
sources.gist: Approved design: dynamic glyph cache, fallback fonts, Twemoji colour emoji keyed by codepoint sequence; three PRs, this is the emoji slice.

sources.label: matemolnar8 on PR #90
sources.author: matemolnar8
sources.body: I would like the golden to contain an emoji and hungarian text. You can merge after that's added and verified.

sources.label: Máté via orchestrator · Oct 25
sources.gist: Do not commit the emoji; download them with the build system into a gitignored folder, and show a fallback character when they are missing.

lookFor: The [proposal](source:s1) lets the longest existing file win for ZWJ, skin tone, flag and keycap clusters. Done; when no prefix longer than one emoji has an image, the cluster draws as its first emoji and the rest of the cluster is swallowed.

The [proposal](source:s1) does not say when a symbol is an emoji. Here a codepoint below U+1F000 is an emoji only when U+FE0F or U+20E3 follows it, so `❤`, `©` and `™`, and emoji-presentation symbols such as `⭐` or `✅` typed without U+FE0F, still draw from the font.

The [proposal's](source:s1) smoke string `Újra 日本語 👍🏽 👨‍👩‍👧 🇭🇺` is not used. The golden draws 🎮 in a Text and 👍 in a Button label; skin tones, ZWJ and flags are covered by `glyph_cache_harness` only, and CJK waits for slice 2.
The [proposal](source:s1) credits Twemoji in the README. Credit is in `assets/emoji/README.md` (shipped in the VPK with the licence) and the SDK README; the root README is unchanged.

The [change request](source:s3) asks for a fallback character. Done differently: a missing image draws the cluster's first codepoint when DejaVu Sans or the Deck App Font has it (so `❤️` stays `❤` and `1️⃣` stays `1`), and `U+FFFD` only when neither does.

Subtle: the pin is the SHA-256 of GitHub's generated tag archive, not a release asset (Twemoji publishes none). If GitHub ever regenerates that zip differently, every fresh configure warns and builds without emoji until the hash is updated.
Manual step: `upload_vita` still FTPs only the eboot, runtime and DejaVu Sans (#93), so a device needs this VPK installed once before emoji appear.

groups.title: Emoji clusters and atlas entries
groups.why: The [design](source:s1) keys emoji by codepoint sequence and loads them into the atlas on demand like glyphs, and the [change request](source:s3) asks for a fallback character when the images are missing.
groups.summary: `vd_emoji_cluster` parses a cluster into a `VdEmojiSequence`, and `glyph_cache_get_emoji` resolves its longest prefix with an image through an injected `VdEmojiLoader`, resampling it into the shared RGBA8 pages, or returns the fallback font glyph when no prefix has one; `glyph_cache_harness` checks both with fake loaders.
lookFor: Perf: the first sight of a (font, size, sequence) reads a file per candidate prefix; a sequence with no image is remembered as a non-colour entry until `glyph_cache_reset`, and those entries are never evicted. With `assets/emoji` empty, each distinct emoji therefore costs one failed `fopen` per prefix once, then hash lookups.
Subtle: an emoji that loads but finds no room this frame is not cached, so its PNG is decoded again on the next frame.

Behaviour change: `glyph_cache_get_emoji` now always returns a glyph for the whole cluster. With no image, 🇭🇺 or 👍🏽 draws one `U+FFFD` instead of two `.notdef` boxes, and `❤️` draws DejaVu Sans's `❤`.
`has_glyph` checks only the requested font and `g_fallback`; it does not go through `glyph_cache_get`'s chain, so a later fallback font (#94) has to be added there too.
`clear_page` now also drops emoji entries that lived on the cleared page.

groups.title: Drawing and measuring by cluster
groups.why: Text, Button and TextInput must draw emoji, and wrapping must not split a cluster ([design](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `text.c` walks clusters instead of codepoints and treats every emoji cluster as one glyph from `glyph_cache_get_emoji`, `render.c` wraps and fits TextInput text by `text_cluster_width`, and `fonts.c` supplies the loader that reads `assets/emoji/<hex-seq>.png` through raylib.
lookFor: Behaviour change: U+200D and U+FE00–U+FE0F now draw nothing and have no width anywhere; before, they drew the font's missing-glyph box.
An emoji is a Font Size square whose top sits at the font's ascent; it advances by Font Size plus the 1 px tracking, and keeps only the text colour's alpha.
The TextInput keep-end fit now measures the whole value once, then drops clusters from the start until the rest fits, because clusters only parse forwards.

groups.title: Twemoji download at configure time
groups.why: Máté picked Twemoji (CC-BY 4.0) for emoji art in the [design](source:s1), and the [change request](source:s3) asks for the images to be downloaded by the build into a gitignored folder, not committed.
groups.summary: `cmake/twemoji.cmake` downloads the v17.0.3 tag zip once, checks its SHA-256, extracts `assets/72x72` into `assets/emoji` without `-fe0f` and writes a stamp, which `.gitignore` hides, the CI workflows cache and the VPK packs; the licence and attribution stay tracked.
lookFor: A failed download or hash mismatch prints a CMake warning, writes no stamp and leaves the build to carry on; the next configure retries. A present stamp skips the network entirely, even when PNGs were deleted by hand.

The download writes into the source tree, not the build directory, so `out`, `out-smoke`, `out-sanitize` and `out-vita` share one copy; Docker runs as root, which is why `smoke-docker.sh` now chowns `assets/emoji`.
`VD_TWEMOJI_DOWNLOADED` makes the harness check a renamed file (`1f3f3-200d-1f308.png`) only when the configure found the stamp.

commits.subject: test(ui): emoji without Twemoji images draw the fallback glyph once
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: feat(ui): emoji without an image draw a fallback glyph
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
An emoji cluster whose Twemoji image is missing, as when the download
failed, now draws once as a whole: its first codepoint from the font or
the Runtime Default Font, else U+FFFD, instead of a .notdef box per
codepoint. Misses stay cached, so no image is looked up twice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: build: download Twemoji at configure time instead of vendoring it
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
cmake/twemoji.cmake fetches the pinned v17.0.3 tag archive once, checks
its SHA-256, extracts only assets/72x72 into the gitignored assets/emoji
and drops -fe0f from the names. A failed download warns and the build
carries on without images. CI caches the folder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(ui): colour emoji in the glyph atlas
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Emoji clusters (single, U+FE0F, skin tones, flags, keycaps, ZWJ) resolve
to the longest Twemoji sequence with an image, resampled to the Font Size
into the RGBA8 atlas pages and drawn untinted. A ZWJ sequence without an
image draws as its first emoji. Word wrap and the TextInput fit keep
clusters whole.

commits.subject: test(smoke): Hungarian and emoji line in the golden
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The smoke header draws "Árvíztűrő tükörfúrógép 🎮", so the golden covers
ő and ű (outside Latin-1) through the glyph cache. The emoji is the
.notdef box until the colour emoji slice. The glyph cache harness checks
every Hungarian letter resolves to a real DejaVu Sans glyph.

Glyphs now rasterise at the exact size instead of scaling a 64 px atlas: sharper edges and unfloored advances, same sizes and positions.

commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: test(ui): glyph cache harness
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Covers hits and misses, size keying, the fallback chain with an ASCII-only DejaVu Sans subset, page fill and eviction, and UTF-8 decoding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat: Button font and fontSize props
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The native Button takes a font name after the label; an unset fontSize passes 0 and the host default of 20 applies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(ui): draw text through the glyph cache with Runtime Default Font fallback
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
TrueType and OpenType fonts load as font bytes instead of a pre-baked 64 px atlas, so startup does no rasterising. Text, Button and TextInput measure and draw through text.c; each frame caches the glyphs it draws, then uploads changed atlas pages once before drawing, because vitaGL copies a whole texture that changes after it was drawn. .fnt and .bdf fonts keep raylib's path. Word-wrap chunking no longer splits a UTF-8 sequence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(ui): on-demand glyph cache over stb_truetype
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Glyphs rasterise at the exact pixel size on first use, keyed by (font, size, codepoint), into 1024x1024 RGBA8 atlas pages (4 MiB, at most 4). When every page is full, the least recently used one not used this frame is cleared. A codepoint the font lacks comes from the fallback font, else the font's .notdef.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: chore(vendor): stb_truetype v1.26, the copy raylib 5.5 compiles
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
raylib builds its copy with STBTT_STATIC and installs no external headers, so the glyph cache needs its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
